latin: Scitur in cabala apertissime cur dei filius cum aqua baptismi uenerit, et spiritus sanctus cum igne.
translation: It is known most clearly in the Kabbalah why the Son of God came with the water of baptism, and the Holy Spirit with fire.
translation_note: 'aqua'/'igne' (water/fire) are, per the note shared with the companion thesis 11>44, standard kabbalistic associations of water with the fourth sefirah and fire with the fifth (paraphrase; farmer1998:27363).
translator: original translation, drafted 2026-09-26 by WRITER-full-batch20, from Latin at farmer1998:27335
attribution: Pico's own opinion (section 11>, Cabalistic conclusions confirming the Christian religion by his own opinion) (farmer1998:27335).
doctrine: Farmer's note, covering theses 11>44-45 together, glosses 'water' as associated with the fourth sefirah, God's love or piety, and 'fire' with the fifth, God's judgment or power (paraphrase; farmer1998:27363). Thesis 11>45 argues that this pairing explains, from within the Kabbalah, why the Son of God came with the water of baptism and the Holy Spirit with fire (farmer1998:27335).
historiography: A German study of Pico's Kabbalistic epistemology cites the thesis alongside 28.13, 11>16, and a Iamblichan conclusion (23.8), referring to Greive's Die christliche Kabbalah and to Wirszubski's Encounter for further discussion (kabbalah_paradigma:2170); the substance of that further discussion, given in German, is not established here.
not_established: The content of the kabbalah_paradigma cross-references beyond the bibliographic note is not established here, the German text not having been translated (kabbalah_paradigma:2170).
